newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom to put shareholder interest first.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom to put shareholder interest first.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG chairman Ron Sommer said on Thursday he agreed with Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Finance Minister Theo Waigel that shareholders' interest should come first in any future share sale.
Sommer said he had discussed the matter personally with Kohl and Waigel.
"We agreed that the interests of shareholders are paramount, and everything else comes after, even if government finances are also important," Sommer told Reuters.

Waigel said on Wednesday the government was considering an early sale of more Telekom shares to help put the budget back on keel. The plan has been sharply criticised by investors who bought shares from the original tranche, which came to market in November.

The government still holds 74 percent of Telekom's 2.7 billion shares, worth about 80 billion marks at current prices. Under current law, it is obligated not to sell any more on stock exchanges before the year 2000.
